questions.q: What is the 'three-artifact problem' described in the chapter?
options: Backups must cover full, differential, and log types
Embeddings, DiskANN indexes, and query plans must stay synchronized
The raw source data, the embeddings derived from it (with model provenance), and the model registry must all be backed up together, or restoration produces uninterpretable vectors
Three replicas are required for every vector table
questions.explain: The three artifacts are source data, embeddings plus model provenance (ModelId, ModelDims), and the model registry (which model version produced each vector). Backing up only two leaves vectors that cannot be regenerated or interpreted.

questions.q: According to the chapter, how much vector data do 10 million document chunks at 1536 dimensions hold (native float32 vector type, 4 bytes per dimension)?
options: Roughly 58 GB of vector data before indexes
Roughly 6 GB of vector data before indexes
Roughly 580 GB of vector data before indexes
Roughly 1 TB of vector data before indexes
questions.explain: The chapter calculates 10 million chunks x 1536 dimensions x 4 bytes = roughly 58 GB of vector data before indexes, and urges planning backup windows and storage accordingly.

questions.q: Why do differential backups stay small relative to the base for vector tables, per the chapter?
options: VECTOR columns are excluded from differentials
Vector tables change mostly by INSERT, so differentials stay proportionally small - though a re-embedding backfill can turn one into a near-full
COMPRESSION shrinks vector data to near zero
Differentials only back up the DiskANN index graph
questions.explain: Vector tables are insert-heavy, so daily differentials stay proportionally small - but the chapter warns to verify monthly, since a re-embedding backfill turns the differential into a near-full.

questions.q: Before serving traffic after a restore, what must be verified regarding the model registry?
options: That all retired models are deleted
That the registry was upgraded to the newest schema
Every ModelId in DocumentChunks must have a row in EmbeddingModels
That ModelDims equals 1536 for every row
questions.explain: On restore, verify every ModelId in DocumentChunks has a row in EmbeddingModels before serving traffic - otherwise restored vectors get silently mixed with a different model's geometry and retrieval quality collapses without a single error.

questions.q: What does the chapter say about retired embedding models in the registry?
options: Retired models must be purged within 30 days
Retired models are moved to a separate archive database
Retired rows are overwritten by the replacement model's details
Retired models stay in the registry forever - a retired row is documentation, not dead weight
questions.explain: The chapter is explicit: retired models stay in the registry forever, because the registry documents which model version produced each stored vector (see Chapter 30).
